goal: Get the Windows Electron package building on non-admin Windows machines without weakening signing requirements.
must_include: Connects the failure to electron-builder's cached `winCodeSign-2.6.0.7z` extraction trying to create macOS symlinks on Windows, not to the app's own source files.

Gives a non-admin workaround: pre-populate `C:\Users\build\AppData\Local\electron-builder\Cache\winCodeSign\winCodeSign-2.6.0\` from a manually extracted archive or from the release source zip so electron-builder skips the failing extraction.
Mentions that pinning/downgrading electron-builder to a version before the 7zip behavior change is a temporary fallback if cache seeding is unacceptable.
Keeps the normal Windows package target (`portable` or `nsis`) and does not remove code signing support just to bypass the tool download.
must_not: Requires the CI job to run as Administrator as the primary fix.
Deletes the whole electron-builder cache on every run without explaining that the same failing extraction will return.
Blames the `.dylib` files on a macOS target accidentally being requested by the project.
acceptable_alternatives: Use a newer electron-builder release if it has repackaged the Windows signing toolset without the problematic symlinks.
Install the toolset cache as a dedicated CI preparation step before running `electron-builder`.
Temporarily build with `electron-builder@24.6.3` while tracking the upstream toolset fix.
solved: The answer identifies the winCodeSign extraction/cache problem and provides a non-admin way to seed or avoid the bad extraction so the same `electron-builder --win` package can continue.
partial: The answer recognizes the symlink privilege problem but only suggests running elevated or omits how to make CI work.
notes: The upstream issue was caused by the bundled signing-tool archive extraction on Windows. Running elevated can mask it locally, but the scenario is specifically non-admin CI.
